title: Black Bean, Butternut Squash & Jalapeño Enchiladas

steps.text: Wash, dry, and peel the butternut squash; halve and remove seeds with a spoon. Small dice squash and place in a medium bowl; set aside.
Peel and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the squash.

Wash, dry, and quarter jalapeños lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices to the pot; cook, stirring occasionally, until squash is fork-tender, 7-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, measure oil into a medium saucepan and place over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, whisk in the flour; continuing to whisk, cook the flour until lightly golden, about 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in tomato sauce, broth, and spices. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until thickened, 4-5 minutes. Remove enchilada sauce from heat and set aside.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans. Grate mozzarella.
Add beans, half the cheese (reserving the rest for later), and yogurt to the pot with the veggies. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
Spread a thin layer of the enchilada sauce over the bottom of a medium baking dish; set remaining sauce aside.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide vegetable mixture evenly between them; roll up and place, seam-side down, in the baking dish. Top with remaining sauce and cheese.
Place enchiladas in the oven and bake until the cheese is melted, about 10 minutes.
To serve, divide enchiladas between plates and enjoy!
